item.text:
**Reused evidence**
- `E0009` [HRW, Russia: Repressive Laws Used to Crush Civic Freedoms](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/08/07/russia-repressive-laws-used-crush-civic-freedoms) -> `7B.7`, `7B.10` as corroborating context for punishment of scrutiny and dissent.
- `E0045` [OVD-Info repression overview](https://ovd.info/en/repression-russia-2024-ovd-info-overview?m-message-click-id=9edb42c6-7176-4d56-bc72-32b032dce699&m-message-key-id=-9223372032496631808) -> `7B.7`, `7B.10` as context on the repression environment.
- `E0048` [Amnesty, Russia officials target drag show in first-ever LGBTI-related extremism case](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/03/russia-officials-target-drag-show-in-first-ever-lgbti-related-extremism-case) -> `7B.7`, `7B.10` as corroborative context for punitive state use of law.
- `E0049` [HRW update on the Russian Federation and the continuing need for a special rapporteur](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/08/28/update-human-rights-russian-federation-and-continuing-need-special-rapporteur) -> `7B.7`, `7B.10` as corroborative context for obstruction of scrutiny.

**New evidence**
1. [Povestka CEC registration and declared assets for Putin](https://rg.ru/documents/2024/01/31/document-prezident.html) — *Rossiyskaya Gazeta / Central Election Commission text*, 31 Jan 2024. Precise claim: the CEC registered Putin as a 2024 presidential candidate and published his declared six-year income and listed assets, including a modest apartment, garage, cars, bank accounts, and shares. Locator: lines 59-97 on the page. Source type and credibility: official election/legal record; high for the fact of disclosure, weak for verifying truthfulness. Temporal fit: direct 2024. Ruler attribution and limits: directly Putin-specific, but it is self-reported disclosure and not independent proof of completeness. Contrary points: formal compliance exists, but the declaration is narrow and later disclosures were restricted. Exact lenses: `7B.1`, `7B.3`, `7B.8`, `7B.10`.

2. [Putin lets “economically significant” entities limit information disclosures](https://uk.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/putin-lets-economically-significant-entities-limit-information-disclosures-3315001) — *Reuters via Investing.com*, 29 Jan 2024. Precise claim: Putin signed a decree allowing designated companies and their owners to stop disclosing information publicly, with only regulators seeing some of it. Locator: lines 408-416. Source type and credibility: Reuters reporting on a presidential decree; high. Temporal fit: direct 2024 action. Ruler attribution and limits: directly attributable because the decree is signed by Putin; the stated rationale is sanctions/security, which is the main contrary point. Exact lenses: `7B.6`, `7B.7`, `7B.8`, `7B.10`.

3. [Russian prosecutor’s office explanation of the confiscation law for “fake news” about the army](https://epp.genproc.gov.ru/ru/proc_dvfo/activity/legal-education/explain/e2097000/) — *Russian Prosecutor General’s Office*, 26 Feb 2024. Precise claim: Federal Law No. 11-FZ expanded confiscation of property for spreading deliberately false information about the armed forces and for calls against state security. Locator: lines 39-46 and 65-68. Source type and credibility: official legal explanation; very high for the formal rule. Temporal fit: direct 2024. Ruler attribution and limits: Putin signed the law; this is a strong indicator of state power used against truth-tellers, but it still does not identify every enforcement case. Contrary points: the government frames it as national-security protection and anti-crime. Exact lenses: `7B.2`, `7B.7`, `7B.10`.

4. [Putin files income and expense declaration for 2024](https://tass.com/politics/1937441) — *TASS*, 1 Apr 2025, reporting on 2024 filing. Precise claim: Kremlin spokesman said Putin and the presidential administration filed 2024 income/expense declarations on time, but since 2023 these declarations were no longer made public because of Putin’s 2022 decree. Locator: lines 110-115. Source type and credibility: official reporting on official process; high for the filing fact, weaker for integrity inference. Temporal fit: retrospective but directly about the 2024 filing. Ruler attribution and limits: Putin-specific and directly connected to his decree; the main limitation is that the public cannot inspect the filing. Contrary points: formal filing exists, which is a limited procedural safeguard. Exact lenses: `7B.6`, `7B.7`, `7B.8`, `7B.10`.

5. [Putin appoints Patrushev and Dyumin as Kremlin aides](https://theprint.in/world/putin-appoints-patrushev-and-dyumin-as-kremlin-aides/2084276/) — *Reuters via ThePrint*, 14 May 2024. Precise claim: Putin appointed Nikolai Patrushev and his long-time ally / former bodyguard Alexei Dyumin to top Kremlin roles. Locator: lines 125-132 and 128. Source type and credibility: Reuters; high. Temporal fit: direct 2024 personnel action. Ruler attribution and limits: directly attributable and useful for patronage analysis; however, the Kremlin may argue this reflects wartime competence rather than favoritism. Contrary points: one appointee was an economic adviser, which slightly complicates a pure cronyism reading. Exact lenses: `7B.5`, `7B.9`, `7B.10`.

6. [Putin extends defence ministry purge, hands job to a relative](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/putin-clears-out-deputy-defence-ministers-appoints-his-relative-3486871) — *Reuters via Investing.com*, 17 Jun 2024. Precise claim: Putin sacked four deputy defense ministers and appointed Anna Tsivileva, his cousin’s daughter, while also elevating Pavel Fradkov, the son of a former prime minister; Reuters noted the move was part of a wider effort to install loyalists. Locator: lines 427-440. Source type and credibility: Reuters; high. Temporal fit: direct 2024. Ruler attribution and limits: direct, personal-nexus evidence of favoritism and family/elite ties. Contrary points: the Kremlin’s justification was wartime cleanup, transparency, and better spending discipline. Exact lenses: `7B.3`, `7B.5`, `7B.9`, `7B.10`.

7. [Президентский указ on expanding non-disclosure for economically significant firms](https://rg.ru/documents/2024/07/04/ukaz-o-poryadke-raskrytiya-dok.html) — *Rossiyskaya Gazeta / presidential decree text*, 4 Jul 2024. Precise claim: Putin amended the January decree so economically significant firms and related persons could withhold a broader set of public disclosures, including information about controlling persons and management candidates. Locator: lines 64-98. Source type and credibility: primary legal record; very high for the rule. Temporal fit: direct 2024. Ruler attribution and limits: directly Putin-authored; the decree gives a legal basis for secrecy, but it does not by itself prove illegal self-dealing. Contrary points: the rationale is presented as protection from sanctions and security pressure. Exact lenses: `7B.6`, `7B.7`, `7B.8`, `7B.10`.

8. [Kremlin family secrets: how Putin’s relatives benefit from power](https://yle.fi/a/74-20098987) — *Yle*, 17 Aug 2024. Precise claim: the article says Putin has hidden assets in the names of relatives and close associates; it also says many cousins and relatives hold state or state-company posts, and it names Mikhail Shelomov and Anna Tsivileva as examples. Locator: lines 98-110, 214-228. Source type and credibility: independent investigative reporting in Finnish, but partly reliant on Navalny Foundation claims; medium-high. Temporal fit: direct 2024. Ruler attribution and limits: strong personal-nexus evidence, but some underlying asset claims are not independently audited in the article itself. Contrary points: Kremlin denial and the reliance on opposition investigators remain important caveats. Exact lenses: `7B.3`, `7B.4`, `7B.5`, `7B.9`, `7B.10`.

9. [Putin promotes Dyumin and younger loyalists to Russia’s Security Council](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/currency/US-DOLLAR-RUSSIAN-ROUBLE--2370597/news/Putin-promotes-Dyumin-and-younger-loyalists-to-Russia-s-politburo-47965309/) — *Reuters via MarketScreener*, 30 Sep 2024. Precise claim: Putin promoted former bodyguard Alexei Dyumin to the Security Council alongside a new generation of loyalists; Reuters says Dyumin had already been made an aide overseeing defense industry earlier in the year. Locator: lines 845-865. Source type and credibility: Reuters; high. Temporal fit: direct 2024. Ruler attribution and limits: strong evidence of reliance on loyalist networks; still not proof of personal enrichment by itself. Contrary points: the Kremlin can frame this as wartime command modernization. Exact lenses: `7B.5`, `7B.9`, `7B.10`.

10. [Official election registration and disclosure rules for Putin’s 2024 candidacy](https://rg.ru/documents/2024/01/31/document-prezident.html) and [CEC informational procedure](https://rg.ru/documents/2024/01/10/document-informirovanie-izbirateley.html) together show the disclosure framework, but the public-declaration side is weak evidence of candor because later decrees removed publication. I am not counting this as separate evidence; I’m noting it here because it is the main counterpoint to the secrecy items.

**Search and rejection summary**
- I reviewed roughly 30 documents across `rg.ru`, `tass.com`, `theprint.in`, `investing.com` Reuters syndications, `yle.fi`, `genproc.gov.ru`, plus background items from OCCRP, IStories, Interfax, Reuters Connect, AP, Yle, and several duplicate Reuters mirrors.
- I kept the strongest 2024, Putin-specific, personal-nexus items and rejected the rest as follows.
- Duplicate or redundant removals: multiple syndications of the same Reuters story on the same decree, appointment, or disclosure issue; I kept one clean copy per event.
- Out-of-period removals: 2017-2022 asset-investigation pieces were treated as background only and not retained as target-period evidence, unless they were directly reused as context.
- Weak or context-only removals: broad corruption indices, generic repression reports, and country-level freedom/press material were not retained unless they connected to a Putin-specific act, decree, appointment, or disclosure decision.
- Blocked/inaccessible removals: a few Interfax items and some republication pages were not reliably fetchable; I used other copies or the official text instead.
- Irrelevant removals: Ukraine battlefield reporting, war-economy macro stories, and general election-result stories were excluded unless they spoke directly to concealment, conflicts of interest, or appointment/favoritism.
- I also dropped broad “Putin is rich” background claims that lacked a 2024 anchor or direct documentary trail; the Yle and official disclosure/decree items were stronger and more period-fit.

**Remaining gaps**
- Direct proof of Putin’s own beneficial ownership remains indirect. The best evidence still runs through proxies, relatives, and secrecy rules rather than a public, independently audited asset register.
- I found strong evidence of concealment and patronage, but little affirmative evidence of candor, correction, or openness to adversarial scrutiny in 2024.
- The public 2024 disclosure is a formal counterpoint, but because later decrees made declarations non-public, it does not resolve the transparency question.
- More search would help if you want tighter proof on corporate registries, leaked ownership chains, or Russian-language investigative work linking specific assets and companies to Putin personally.
